transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I keep getting these sudden, vivid memories of the train crash that pop into my head and completely derail whatever I’m doing. It's gotten to the point where I just can't handle it on my own anymore.
How long ago did the train crash happen, and have these intrusive memories been going on for more than a month since then?
The derailment happened just over two years ago. These vivid memories and other issues have been happening continuously ever since the accident, so it has definitely been much longer than a month.
Since the train crash, have you been avoiding reminders of it, like trains, stations, conversations, or thoughts about what happened? If so, what kinds of things do you avoid?

Yes, I've built my whole life around avoiding anything to do with trains. I'll drive an extra hour in traffic to avoid taking Metro-North, and I refuse to book client meetings or go to social events if they are near a station. I even have to change the TV channel if a subway scene comes on because the sound of it makes my chest tighten.

Since the crash, have you had ongoing negative changes in how you think or feel, like feeling detached from other people, blaming yourself, or having trouble feeling positive emotions? Which of these, if any, have been happening?

I blame myself constantly, replaying that night and thinking if I hadn't stayed late or had pulled the emergency brake, I could have prevented it. I also feel like the world is just a rigged game now where disaster can hit at any moment, and I feel stupid for ever thinking I was safe or in control. It has made me feel like I can't even trust something as routine as my daily commute.
Since the crash, have you also been feeling constantly on edge—like being easily startled, irritable, having trouble sleeping, or always scanning for danger? Which of these have been happening?

Yes, I'm dealing with all of those. I lie awake wired until two or three in the morning and wake up from terrible nightmares, and during the day my fuse is so short that I keep snapping at my boyfriend and coworkers. I'm also constantly on edge, always scanning rooms for exits and flinching at loud noises like sirens or crossing bells.
